key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation and neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects and stabilize thermal and axial-force responses in HDPE joining.
method: Developed an experimentally validated 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defects.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Combined simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding windows.
evidence_signal: ANN predictions achieved R² of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N and raised peak temperature from 70 °C to about 100 °C.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated within the tested parameter space; extrapolation to other HDPE grades, tool geometries or welding conditions requires validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
